thread:
Sophia Li: Quick check — planning to enable feature flag `burst_queueing_v2` for a canary tonight. thinking 5% traffic -> 20% -> full over 2 hours. Any objections?

Michael Chen: 5% sounds fine. what's the canary audience? internal only or a subset of customers?

Sophia Li: Stage 1 = internal (all dev and staging), Stage 2 = 5% of prod routed to region-us-east-1 users, Stage 3 = 20% after OK. canary will be targeted by account_id hashing.

Anna Rodrigues: Add guardrail: if p95 latency increases by > 25% vs baseline or queue_length > 200 for >3min, auto-disable. we should wire that into the rollout job.

Rav Patel: Agree on guardrails. Also add a max_concurrency cap per worker while canary is on: `max_concurrency: 8` (was 16). avoids overwhelming backends.

Michael Chen: Where's the runbook? link please.

Sophia Li: Runbook: https://redwood-internal/ops/runbooks/burst-queueing-v2 — includes rollback steps and dashboards to watch (p50/p95/p99 latency, queue_length, free_gpus).

Anna Rodrigues: Pinged the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123 — config lives in `deploy/flags/burst_queueing_v2.yaml`. small snippet:```yaml
name: burst_queueing_v2
enabled: false
canary:
  stages:
    - name: internal
      percent: 0
    - name: prod-5
      percent: 5
    - name: prod-20
      percent: 20
guardrails:
  latency_increase_pct: 25
  queue_length_max: 200
  max_concurrency_override: 8
```

Rav Patel: Nice. For the auto-disable action, make sure the toggle flips to `enabled: false` and we post to #incidents and create a short alert ticket.

deploy-bot: Notice: scheduled rollout job created for 2024-11-05T02:00:00Z. job_id=job-8892.

Sophia Li: Can someone from oncall be available during the 1st stage (internal -> prod-5)? ideally @oncall-rotations for the window.

oncall-rotations: I can take the first 90m watch. will escalate to SRE if any anomalies. Please provide the baseline dashboard link.

Michael Chen: Baseline dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/abcd/burst-queueing-baseline?orgId=1
Also: quick toggle command if we need to kill:```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"burst_queueing_v2","enabled":false}' \
  https://api.redwood-internal/flags/toggle
```

Anna Rodrigues: Two asks before we flip: 1) confirm load test from yesterday (rps spike sim) passed and there were no memory regressions; 2) make sure KV cache TTLs are preserved under queueing mode.

Sophia Li: Load test results are in the PR comments — passing, small p99 tail increase ~4%. KV cache TTLs unchanged per the runtime test logs.

Rav Patel: Reminder: set `burst_scope: "region-us-east-1"` for the first prod stage so we don't hit other regions.

Sophia Li: yeah will set that in job config. also will include a quick smoke that runs warmup requests and checks KV hit rate > 60% before opening to prod-5.

Michael Chen: If all agree, i can flip internal today at 22:00 PT, and open prod-5 at 02:00 UTC. I'll leave a postmortem template ready if anything goes sideways.

Anna Rodrigues: 👍 from me. make sure to tag #support and #customer-success if we touch any enterprise customers during canary.

Sophia Li: thank you all. final plan: internal at 22:00 PT (today), monitor 30m -> prod-5 at 02:00 UTC; guardrails as listed; kill-switch curl available; oncall watching. I'll update the PR and the rollout job.

Rav Patel: small nit: include `max_queue_wait_ms: 5000` as a soft cap so we don't increase tail lat too much.

Sophia Li: added. I'll post back here with job run id and the first-stage metrics snapshot after internal run. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Job started: job-8892 stage=internal at 2024-11-05T22:00:00Z

Sophia Li: internal stage looks clean after 30m. p95 +3%, queue_length steady ~40. moving to prod-5 at 02:00 UTC per plan.

oncall-rotations: on watch. will call out immediately if queue_length climbs or error rate > 1%.

Michael Chen: prod-5 now live. monitoring dashboard.

Sophia Li: so far so good. keeping this thread open for post-rollout notes and any follow ups.

Anna Rodrigues: after full rollout let's schedule a short retro to capture learnings and update the runbook with the `max_queue_wait_ms` default.

Rav Patel: noted. thanks everyone.
